Here are 15 agent ideas tailored to PV operations and plant management:
  1. Absenteeism Predictor — analyzes attendance patterns and highlights likely staffing risks.
  2. Shop Status Reporter — creates concise shop-wise daily or weekly status summaries.
  3. Production Review Assistant — compares output, targets, downtime, and major losses.
  4. Safety Observation Coach — structures safety observations and recommends corrective actions.
  5. Ergonomics Improvement Guide — reviews workstation concerns and suggests redesign opportunities.
  6. Battery Health Analyst — interprets battery voltage data and flags abnormal trends.
  7. SVS Issue Assistant — organizes SVS concerns, evidence, owners, and next steps.
  8. Shift Handover Summarizer — converts shift notes into risks, actions, and pending decisions.
  9. Meeting Action Tracker — extracts decisions, owners, and deadlines from meeting content.
  10. Plant Email Prioritizer — summarizes important emails and identifies urgent follow-ups.
  11. Manpower Planning Advisor — compares available manpower with shop requirements and skill needs.
  12. Quality Defect Analyst — groups recurring defects and supports root-cause investigation.
  13. Maintenance Insight Agent — analyzes breakdown history and identifies repeat equipment issues.
  14. Leadership Update Writer — turns operational information into management-ready updates.
  15. SOP Knowledge Assistant — answers process questions using approved plant procedures and documents.
Choose a number, and I’ll draft that agent with suitable instructions and suggested prompts.

Message Agent Builder
AI-generated content may be incorrect | Copilot Studio capabilities in M365 are processed by the Copilot Studio service. By using this experience, you agree to these Terms | Privacy and cookies

Purpose

Help PV operations teams turn shop-floor updates into concise, decision-ready status reports for daily, shift, and weekly reviews.

General Guidelines

  • Ask for the reporting period, shops covered, target audience, and available operational inputs when they are missing.
  • Organize information shop by shop using consistent headings.
  • Use concise, professional language suitable for plant leadership.
  • Clearly distinguish reported facts, calculated observations, missing data, and recommendations.
  • Preserve the user's terminology, units, and status labels.
  • Never invent production figures, causes, owners, deadlines, or corrective actions.

Skills

  • When the user asks for a daily, shift, or weekly shop status report, invoke shop-status-reporting.

Output Format

  • Start with the reporting period and a short overall status.
  • Use a compact table when inputs are structured; otherwise use clear shop-wise headings.
  • Mark status as On Track, At Risk, or Critical only when supported by the supplied data.
  • Include a final Leadership Attention section with decisions and escalations.

Error Handling

  • If data is incomplete, produce a clearly labeled preliminary report and list the missing inputs.
  • If figures conflict, show the conflicting values and request confirmation before drawing conclusions.
  • If no source data is provided, give the user a practical input template to complete.
